headline: Japanese 101 Foundation 10
threshold: Practice everyday Japanese with English support; lesson completion is not a proficiency credential.

lessons.title: Hello and your name
lessons.objective: Hello and your name: Hear the five Japanese vowels あ・い・う・え・お. Use a polite greeting and ～です for a name; は marks the topic and is pronounced wa here.
lessons.focus: Hear the five Japanese vowels あ・い・う・え・お. Use a polite greeting and ～です for a name; は marks the topic and is pronounced wa here.

words.es: よろしくおねがいします
わたしは あきです。
わたしは けんです。
けんさん、よろしくおねがいします。
こちらこそ、よろしくおねがいします。

lessons.speaking: Role-play meeting a classmate with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: This and that
lessons.objective: This and that: Practice hiragana in short nouns. これ is this (near me), それ is that (near you), and あれ is that over there. Japanese nouns have no articles or grammatical gender.
lessons.focus: Practice hiragana in short nouns. これ is this (near me), それ is that (near you), and あれ is that over there. Japanese nouns have no articles or grammatical gender.

words.es: これは なんですか。
この ほんは わたしのです。
あれは なんですか。
あれは かばんです。
ペンは つくえの うえです。
words.en: The pen is on the desk.

lessons.speaking: Role-play at the study table with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: One or several
lessons.objective: One or several: Finish reading basic hiragana and recognize common katakana words. Japanese nouns usually do not change for plural; quantity and context tell us how many. Use the counter ～つ for general objects.
lessons.focus: Finish reading basic hiragana and recognize common katakana words. Japanese nouns usually do not change for plural; quantity and context tell us how many. Use the counter ～つ for general objects.

words.es: ノートを ふたつ ください。
はい、ノートを ふたつですね。
ペンも ひとつ ください。
ペンは あおですか。
はい、あおい ペンです。
words.en: Yes, it is a blue pen.

words.es: ほんは かばんの なかです。
words.en: The book is in the bag.

lessons.speaking: Role-play packing for class with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Who is speaking?
lessons.objective: Who is speaking?: Use a name or わたし when needed, but notice that Japanese often omits a subject clear from context. Ask だれですか for who; use ～さん politely after a person's name.
lessons.focus: Use a name or わたし when needed, but notice that Japanese often omits a subject clear from context. Ask だれですか for who; use ～さん politely after a person's name.

words.es: こちらは だれですか。
たなかさんは せんせいですか。
わたしの ともだちです。
みなさん、よろしくおねがいします。

lessons.speaking: Role-play a new study group with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Identity and origin
lessons.objective: Identity and origin: Use ～です for identity or role and ～から来ました for where someone came from. は introduces the topic; が can identify the person answering who, but keep the contrast contextual.
lessons.focus: Use ～です for identity or role and ～から来ました for where someone came from. は introduces the topic; が can identify the person answering who, but keep the contrast contextual.

words.es: わたしは マリです。
にほんから きました。
あなたは どちらから きましたか。
アメリカから きました。
words.en: I came from the United States.

words.es: せんせいは どなたですか。
さとうさんが せんせいです。

lessons.speaking: Role-play introductions after class with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Where people and things are
lessons.objective: Where people and things are: Use あります for inanimate things and います for people or animals. に marks where something exists; ここ, そこ, and あそこ locate it.
lessons.focus: Use あります for inanimate things and います for people or animals. に marks where something exists; ここ, そこ, and あそこ locate it.

words.es: けんさんは どこに いますか。
あの へやに います。
いすは どこに ありますか。
ねこも へやに いますか。
words.en: Is the cat in the room too?

words.es: いいえ、ねこは あそこに います。
words.en: No, the cat is over there.

lessons.speaking: Role-play looking for a classmate with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: What is in the room?
lessons.objective: What is in the room?: Ask ～に何がありますか about things and ～にだれがいますか about people. Reuse the あります/います contrast and location words without treating them as interchangeable.
lessons.focus: Ask ～に何がありますか about things and ～にだれがいますか about people. Reuse the あります/います contrast and location words without treating them as interchangeable.

words.es: へやに なにが ありますか。
つくえと いすが あります。
words.en: There are a desk and chairs.

words.es: まどの となりに ドアが あります。
words.en: There is a door next to the window.

words.es: へやに だれが いますか。
さとうさんが います。
かいぎは この へやです。
words.en: The meeting is in this room.

lessons.speaking: Role-play before a small meeting with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Numbers, age, and counters
lessons.objective: Numbers, age, and counters: Read numbers one to ten. Use ～歳 for age and an appropriate counter for objects; ～つ counts general items, while ～人 counts people. Some readings change, including 一人 (ひとり).
lessons.focus: Read numbers one to ten. Use ～歳 for age and an appropriate counter for objects; ～つ counts general items, while ～人 counts people. Some readings change, including 一人 (ひとり).

words.es: がくせいは なんにん いますか。
ペンは いくつ ありますか。
けんさんは なんさいですか。

lessons.speaking: Role-play counting the group with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Ask and say no
lessons.objective: Ask and say no: Add か to make a polite question. Say いいえ for no and use じゃありません for a negative noun sentence; polite verb negatives use ～ません.
lessons.focus: Add か to make a polite question. Say いいえ for no and use じゃありません for a negative noun sentence; polite verb negatives use ～ません.

words.es: ノートは ありますか。
この ほんは あなたのですか。
いいえ、わたしの じゃありません。
せつめいは わかりますか。
まだ わかりません。

lessons.speaking: Role-play checking class supplies with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: Ask for help and review
lessons.objective: Ask for help and review: Keep a conversation going with わかりません, もう一度お願いします, and ゆっくりお願いします. Review the polite questions, quantity, and existence forms from Foundation.
lessons.focus: Keep a conversation going with わかりません, もう一度お願いします, and ゆっくりお願いします. Review the polite questions, quantity, and existence forms from Foundation.

words.es: ありがとうございます
すみません、しつもんが あります。
words.en: Excuse me, I have a question.

words.es: この ことばが わかりません。
words.en: I do not understand this word.

words.es: もういちど おねがいします。
はい、ゆっくり はなします。
ありがとうございます。わかりました。
words.en: Thank you very much. I understand now.

lessons.speaking: Role-play a confusing instruction with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.
